texts.facts: 2. The Writ Petitioners herein were originally appointed as Health Inspectors under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act and they were governed by the concerned local bodies. Later, when the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 came into force, the petitioners were directed to act as Food Safety Officers under the new Act from 2011 onwards. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 3. The Medical Services Recruitment Board had issued a recruitment notification on 13.10.2021. In notification dated 13.10.2021, applications have been called for, for the appointment of Food Safety Officers by way of direct recruitment and pursuant to the said notification, several candidates have applied and a provisional selection list was published. Later, a revised provisional selection list was published on 21.08.2024, which is under challenge in the present Writ Petition.
texts.arguments: 4. The apprehension of the Writ Petitioners is that though they are working as Food Safety Officers from the year 2011 onwards, unless their service conditions are settled by the Government, their seniority would be affected. 5. The learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the first respondent herein has contended that service conditions were framed for the Food Safety Officers under G.O.Ms.No.438, Health and Family Welfare (M1) Department, dated 24.09.2018 and the same came into force on 24.09.2018 itself. Thereafter, an amendment in the Service Rules was issued under G.O.Ms.No.201, Health and Family Welfare (M1) Department, dated https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 30.06.2022, wherein Rule 10 was inserted. As per the said Rule, nothing in the Service Rules, shall adversely affect the persons holding the post of Food Safety Officers on the date of publication of these Rules. Therefore, according to the learned Additional Advocate General, the recruitment of the Food Safety Officers under the notification of the Medical Services Recruitment Board, would not in any way affect the services of the Writ Petitioners, who are already working as Food Safety Officers. 6. The learned Additional Advocate General also relied upon the counted filed by the Commissioner of Food Safety, Chennai, especially paragraph 13, which is extracted as follows: 13. It is further submitted that the 2nd respondent has published the revised provisional selection list, pursuant to the direction of the Honble High Court in Contempt Petition No.868 of 2024. Considering the provisional selection list and issuing appointment orders to the selected candidates would not affect the service conditions of the existing Food Safety Officers, since their absorption and seniority related matters are pending at the government https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 7.
